title: Inside the creator economy's AI reckoning
tldr: AI shifted from something creators feared to a widely adopted strategy, reshaping how content gets made in the creator economy. Signals a major mindset flip worth tracking.
why_fresh: documents a genuine sentiment shift in creator economy
angle: Write about the emotional arc of creators from AI-anxiety to AI-adoption and what it means for authenticity.

title: Beyond Communications: How Internal Comms Can Redesign the Employee Experience
tldr: Argues internal comms' job is shifting from 'did employees see the message' to 'did we make work easier.' Reframes internal comms as experience design.
why_fresh: new framing of internal comms role
angle: Explore internal comms as employee experience design rather than message distribution.

title: Three in four Americans use smartphones while watching TV
tldr: New data shows 75% of Americans second-screen while watching TV, reshaping how attention and content consumption actually works. Direct evidence on media-consumption habits.
angle: What second-screening means for content strategy—design for divided attention, not immersion.

title: A billboard of signed school leavers' shirts carrying testimony of AI-enabled harm
tldr: Don't Panic's campaign for Everyone's Invited pins real school shirts with handwritten testimonies to a billboard—raw, human-first campaign craft. A striking case study in people-over-polish storytelling.
angle: Break down why real handwritten testimony beats polished creative for emotional impact.

title: The Atlantic is getting more subscribers from Google traffic, even as referrals fall
tldr: The Atlantic's Google referrals dropped but subscriber conversions from Google rose—fewer, higher-intent visitors. Reframes the 'Google Zero' panic for publishers.
why_fresh: counterintuitive fresh data on traffic quality
angle: Argue that quality of traffic beats quantity in the AI-search era—and what content teams should optimize for.

title: The AI content tsunami: Creation is the easy part
tldr: With AI making content creation trivial, the hard work shifts to distribution, governance and standing out. Reframes where content teams should invest.
angle: If creation is free, what becomes scarce? Make the case for distribution and curation as the new moats.

title: Nearly all luxury resale transactions on TikTok Shop US now come from livestreams
tldr: 94% of TikTok Shop US luxury resale revenue in 2026 comes from livestreaming—a striking concentration in live commerce. Shows where a format is winning.
angle: Livestreaming as storytelling: why live human sellers convert where static listings fail.

title: Sonos' brand repositioning trades specs for vibes in hunt for comeback
tldr: Sonos pivots from audiophile specs to emotion and experience to recover from a product misstep. A clean case study in emotional brand repositioning.
angle: When to trade specs for feelings—and the risk of vibes without proof.

title: Why external comms can't succeed without internal alignment
tldr: Argues internal and external comms must sync or announcements get messy and damage reputation. Practical governance angle for communicators.
angle: How to build an internal-first announcement workflow so employees never learn news from the press.

title: How to break through social media saturation in a world of overwhelm
tldr: Calls time on 'content for content's sake' and argues for restraint and human resonance amid audience overwhelm. Speaks to a real consumption-fatigue shift.
angle: Less-but-better: making the case for volume cuts and human-centered posting.

title: Gen Z doesn't trust anyone—especially their bosses, data shows
tldr: Only 13% of Gen Z say most people can be trusted, the least trusting generation on record. Big implications for internal comms and leadership credibility.
angle: Communicating to a low-trust generation: why transparency and peer voices beat corporate polish.

title: Martha Stewart on the Power of Human Expertise in the Age of AI
tldr: Stewart's new venture Hint bets on human curation and judgment as AI reshapes how consumers decide. A high-profile human-over-machine positioning play.
angle: Why credentialed human expertise becomes a premium content asset as AI floods the zone.

title: How Facebook's News Feed introduced the age of the algorithm 20 years ago
tldr: A 20-year retrospective on how the News Feed reshaped media consumption and everyday life. Useful long-view context for content strategists.
angle: What two decades of algorithmic feeds taught us—and what the AI-answer era might repeat.

title: Lost in translation: Why content and data teams can't speak the same language
tldr: Explores the persistent gap between content and analytics teams and how to bridge it. Relevant to content ops and measurement alignment.
angle: A shared vocabulary for content and data teams—translating stories into metrics and back.
